JASS contributed to the design of security recommendations during a visit to one of the most conflict-sensitive areas in Guatemala alongside partners. As part of building and designing these recommendations, JASS, as part of the coalition (50+), attended the mission that lasted 3 days. JASS facilitated conversations between the land defenders, a women's rights centre and the National Ombudsman to seek a specific safe space for women to share their experiences and centre their struggles by facilitating interviews and other mechanisms of data collection for the purposes designing security recommendations.In 2023, JASS accompanied a partner during a corruption trial that allowed for extractivism from a river without legal rights. By providing this support, the partner was able to:•Feel safe during the legal proceedings•Feel prepared and aware of what would happen •Share and process the ongoing proceedings with a critical friend""•Through this accompaniment, JASS was able to:•Strengthen facilitator's skills•Strengthen the capacity to deliver Feminist Popular Education•Strengthen women's leadership""•Through this accompaniment, JASS was able to:•Strengthen facilitator's skills•Strengthen the capacity to deliver Feminist Popular Education•Strengthen women's leadership""In partnership with a new ally, JASS created a platform to receive complaints for land violations (such as evictions without consent). The purpose of this platform is to:1.Collect information to challenge power holders2.Use the information provided to run campaigns and create communication products for distribution3.Bring attention to human rights violations and violence against women During 2023, there were a string of evictions and those who stood against them were victims of violence, including the attempted murder of Miriam Miranda. The campaign results of 2023 were:1.Brought attention to the violations and related violence 2.Places pressure on power holders at the judicial and executive level to stop this wave of evictions3.Places pressure on power holders to stop criminalization of those defending their landThrough the political accompaniment of the partner, JASS supported a new context analysis to be conducted as part of informing the next strategy for the partner. The partner continues to participate in Alquimia school, which gives them the practical tools and methods for movement building. JASS also follows up on their movement building, in order to strengthen it. For 2024, JASS is supporting the partner to be part of an exchange with the Nobel Women's Initiative to strengthen their advocacy communication. As part of JASS' political accompaniment, the partner works with JASS to exchange advocacy and communications, particularly advocacy at the community level. As part of the link between Feminist Movement Building and Racial Justice, JASS political accompaniment of this organisation has resulted in a strengthened political analysis of the racial impacts in movements. The partner also had facilitators participate in JASS' Alquimia school for feminist popular education facilitation which has resulted in the organsation’s movement strengthening, and use of new tools and methodologies for movement building.Land defenders were equipped with methodological tools and practices to support their well-being through ""heart-mind-body"" techniques which are about connecting breathe, mindfulness and activism as a method of self-care. As captured in the MTR, WHRDs are at high-risk of burnout and thus JASS is focusing on tools that can foster self and collective care. The tools are useful for all ages and women have shared that they have used it to facilitate their healing journeys and to decolonize narratives about wellness practices. Although the tool has not directly influenced any agenda setting process it has influenced debate on wellbeing being a political practice and the importance of equally linking to the sustainability of our movements to self and collective care.

These new partnerships with power holders have demonstrated the power of art as a tool for lobby and advocacy and the development of partnerships with unlikely stakeholders.

Total 40 WHRDs and 39 where new, Political facilitators were provided with methodological and analytical tools that strengthened their capacities to become women leaders, facilitators and better popular educators within their movements. As a result, as Feminist Popular Education facilitators, they have the knowledge and skill to harness women's individual and collective power through Feminist Movement Building processes using Feminist Popular Education.JASS convened a dialogue with Alquimia land defenders in order to exchange ideas and experiences. After the dialogue WHRDs were able to:•provide critical analysis of their current territorial struggles including highlighting its current relevance.•recognize the crucial role women play in the protection of territories and human rights; and•examine of how movements face cultural narrative against dispossession when trying to claim their rights.As a result:•Women had the skills to develop collective strategic plans •Conduct agenda setting•Develop safety and protection strategies as a collective2023 was the last phase of the Alquimia Political Facilitators School. The process has strengthened women's leadership and transformative power through both theoretical and practical methodologies based on feminist popular education. Topics from the school include •Analysis of Systems of Oppression, •Extractivisms, •Women's Movements and Resistance, •Influence and Advocacy, •Comprehensive Feminist Protection and, •Transformation Conflict.As a result, women leaders became more actively involved in civic issues such as the political situation that arose after the elections (the coup). The political facilitators were part of the movement denouncing, resisting and coordinating to strengthen the peaceful resistance in defense of democracy in Guatemala. In the last two months of 2023, the ancestral authorities of the different towns called for a demonstration and peaceful resistance to defend the rule of law. There was a strong participation of the political facilitators and their movements who were leading mobilizations of women on the streets, denunciation actions, and challenging power holders. JASS conducted two Feminist Movement Builders schools with Garifunaarifuna and Mayan women from Izabal. They are activists and defenders of ancestral knowledge, land and territory. As a result of the feminist movement builders' school, women strengthened their political analysis skills, better understood their current context and learned about tools and methodologies for movement building. This resulted in new strategies for the women to use when defending against extractivism in their communities (particularly around new power/electricity projects).
